names.display_en: Li Xiong, Grand Ancestor of Cheng Han

summary: 巴氐流民首领李特之子，继统部众，称成都王、即帝位，国号大成，都成都；在位三十年，赋役较轻、蜀人安之，为十六国中最善治者之一。
summary_en: Son of the Ba-Di refugee leader Li Te, he took over the host, styled himself King of Chengdu, then emperor of the realm Dacheng with its capital at Chengdu; in thirty years of light levies and easy rule the Shu people were content — one of the most benign of the Sixteen States' sovereigns.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现宽厚有度的开国之君之态，衣冠从成汉制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary: 巴氐李特子，字仲俊。随特入蜀。
timeline.summary_en: Son of the Ba-Di leader Li Te, styled Zhongjun; he followed Te into Shu.

timeline.title: 继统流民军
timeline.summary: 李特死，雄继统部众，与罗尚等相攻。
timeline.summary_en: Li Te died; Xiong took command and fought Luo Shang and the others.

timeline.title: 称成都王
timeline.summary: 即成都王位，建元，成汉政权成形。
timeline.summary_en: He took the title King of Chengdu, opened an era, and the Cheng Han state took shape.

timeline.title: 称帝
timeline.summary: 即皇帝位，国号大成，都成都。
timeline.summary_en: He took the imperial throne, styled the realm Dacheng, and made Chengdu his capital.

timeline.title: 宽政安蜀
timeline.summary: 史称赋役较轻，蜀人安之。
timeline.summary_en: The histories record light levies and corvée, and the people of Shu at peace.

timeline.title: 李雄崩
timeline.summary: 崩，兄子班继，旋政变，成汉中衰。
timeline.summary_en: He died; his nephew Ban succeeded and was at once overthrown — the decline of Cheng Han began.

relations.note: 与东晋并世，成汉后为桓温所灭
relations.note_en: Contemporary with Eastern Jin; Cheng Han is later destroyed by Huan Wen

meta.inclusion_reason: 成汉开国君主，偏安巴蜀，图鉴以准帝收录。

bio_md:
# 成汉太宗 · 主要事迹

李雄字仲俊，巴氐流民首领李特之子。太安二年，李特与益州刺史罗尚相攻，兵败被杀；雄继统部众，与罗尚等相持。建兴元年，雄称成都王，建元；晏平元年，即皇帝位，国号大成，都成都。成汉遂与中原诸国并立，为十六国中偏安巴蜀者。

李雄在位三十年，史称其「宽政安蜀」：轻徭薄赋，刑狱宽简，「赋役俱省，民庶丰溢」，蜀人安之。雄无子，养兄李荡之子班为太子；玉衡二十四年，雄崩，兄子班继位。然李雄诸子不服，李期等发动政变杀班自立，成汉自此中衰——雄之宽政，未能传之后嗣。

史家评李雄：「雄以宽仁之量，抚流移之民，故能据有巴蜀，垂三十年。」在十六国暴君辈出之际，李雄之治实属难得；然传位不明、诸子争立，其宽政终成昙花一现。成汉后为东晋桓温所灭，偏安之局遂终。

> 参考：点校本《晋书》卷121《李雄载记》、卷120《李特载记》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Li Xiong, styled Zhongjun, was the son of Li Te, leader of the Ba-Di refugee host. In the 2nd year of Tai'an, Li Te, fighting the Yi Province governor Luo Shang, was defeated and slain; Xiong took command and held off Luo Shang. In the 1st year of Jianxing he styled himself King of Chengdu and opened an era; in the 1st year of Yanping he took the imperial throne, styling the realm Dacheng with its capital at Chengdu. Cheng Han stood beside the states of the Central Plains — the one of the Sixteen that held Bashu alone.

In thirty years Xiong's rule was the most benign of the age: light levies, easy justice, "tax and corvée both spared, the people prosperous," and the people of Shu at peace. He had no son and raised his nephew Ban as heir; when he died in the 24th year of Yuheng and Ban succeeded, Xiong's own sons would not bear it — Li Qi and the others murdered Ban, and Cheng Han began its decline. His benevolence could not bequeath itself.

The historians say: "With a measure of benevolence Xiong nourished the refugees, and so held Bashu for nearly thirty years." Amid the tyrants of the Sixteen States his rule stands out; but the succession was unsecured and his sons tore the state — the good rule was a brief spring. Huan Wen of Eastern Jin later destroyed Cheng Han, and the enclave ended.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 121 (records of Li Xiong), ch. 120 (records of Li Te).
